Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 18.10.2023
passed by the Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C. and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Humnabad [for
short 'Tribunal'], in Mvc No.102/2021, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.  One Kishan met with an accident on 31.10.2020 and died.
His wife and children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.
The Tribunal considered the entire materials on record and awarded Rs.18,02,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, claimants filed this appeal.

3. The main contention of the claimants is that the deceased was working as Coolie and earning Rs.26,000/- per month, but the Tribunal considered the income on the lower side and awarded meagre compensation under all NC: 2025:KHC-K:6793 HC-KAR heads.
Therefore, they pray for enhancement of the compensation.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and it needs no interference.

5. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
6.
Deceased was aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Though, it is stated that deceased was earning Rs.26,000/- per month, but not produced any document to prove the same.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.13,750/- per month, for the accident of the year 2020, which needs no interference,

However, as deceased was aged 45 years at the time of accident,
25% future prospects is to be awarded as per NC: 2025:KHC-K:6793 HC-KAR law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance CO. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1.

entities.text: National Insurance CO. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly,
25% of Rs.13,750/- comes to Rs.3,438/-, thus, total income of the deceased comes to Rs.17,188/-.
Out of this amount, if 1/4th is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the claimants entitled for 3/4th of the income.

Thus, the loss of dependency comes to: Rs.17,188/- x 12 x 14 x 3/4 = Rs.21,65,688/-.
7.

For loss of spousal consortium to the wife, loss of parental consortium to the children and filial consortium to the parents of the deceased, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.44,000/- to each, in total Rs.2,64,000/-.
8. The claimants are also entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads as per the citation in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.24,59,688/- as against Rs.18,02,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.
There will be enhancement of Rs.6,57,188/-.
The Insurance Company already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

10. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed.

(ii) The appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,57,188/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced compensation of Rs.6,57,188/- with interest at 6% per annum, within four weeks from the date of this judgment.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6793 HC-KAR (iv) On such deposit, only claimant No.1/appellant No.1 is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
